source_span: the issue is simply a repricing of the cost of capital ... You either cut capex, delay deployment or increasingly fund through equity. None are particularly supportive of equity prices.
source_chain: AI names sold off hard (worst relative day vs. SPX ex-AI) even as results confirmed demand (Bloom Energy, WDC beat-and-raise) therefore the real driver isn't demand but a repricing of the cost of capital funding the buildout therefore issuers are left with three bad options — cut capex, delay deployment, or fund via equity — none of which support share prices; invalidation/test is next week's hyperscaler earnings, specifically how backlog converts to revenue, deployment pace, and what they say about funding.
pulse_chain: Meta's beat confirmed AI ad demand and the stock still fell with its CDS widening, and WDC's ~20% guidance beat still reversed, therefore (per Goldman's Privorotsky) the mechanism is funding, not products: the selloff reprices the cost of capital paying for the buildout, leaving issuers three choices — cut spending, delay deployment, or raise equity — none of which support share prices; invalidation is next week's hyperscaler reports, per Privorotsky testing backlog-to-revenue conversion, deployment pace, and funding commentary.
why: The pulse keeps the same three-choice capital-repricing argument attributed correctly to Goldman's Privorotsky, in the same direction, with the same hyperscaler-earnings invalidation condition, adding only compression and supporting figures from other sources rather than altering or reversing a step.
